text.p: Sprint Corp. Thursday reported lower earnings for the second quarter, citing tougher competition in the long distance telephone business.
It earned $256.0 million, or 59 cents a share, down from year-earlier earnings of $317.0 million, or 73 cents a share. Revenues rose to $3.67 billion from $3.47 billion.
Following the news, Sprint's stock fell 50 cents to $46 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Sprint said its second-quarter earnings included a $20 million charge to settle a class action lawsuit.
Long distance revenues rose 8.1 percent to $2.2 billion, and local phone revenues were up 5.1 percent to $1.35 billion.
